_what: The act slides for Seven Days to the Wolves. One card per act of the programme, in the owner's canonical order, each carrying its Roman numeral. `kind: "act"` is the cinematic handoff slide from the website (CinematicTransition.vue), rendered full-frame by tools/fullframe.py.
_order: The canonical order is the owner's. Given first as 'intro -> endlessdaysmostbeautiful -> mrbobbytables -> kat -> nat -> 7daystothewolves -> europa -> end credits', then amended: 'add osiris before europa and after nat', placed between nat and the musical. So the acts are I intro, II endlessdaysmostbeautiful, III mrbobbytables, IV kat, V nat, VI osiris, VII 7daystothewolves, VIII europa, IX end credits. The numbering is the point: 'add these as the canonical acts of the entire musical - Give them Huge Roman numbers in the intro slides, each will have chapters.'
_copy: Chapter card copy is REPRODUCED, never authored. Where an act has no authored title, the row is omitted rather than filled -- see `unresolved`. The only strings the owner wrote for this pass are act II's title and the whole of act IV's terminal block, both quoted back verbatim.
_chapters: Every act is to carry chapters. None have been authored yet, so every `chapters` list is empty: the field renders nothing until somebody writes the words. An empty list is the recorded gap, not a placeholder to fill in.
_gaps: Acts II, III and IX have no film in this programme and therefore no card: a slide announcing an act that does not play is worse than a recorded gap. They keep their numerals in `unresolved` so the numbering cannot drift when they are built. III is the one that CHANGED: the Curse of Osiris contributors piece used to stand in for it, and the owner has now given that film its own act (VI), saying of act III 'I will deal with it later'.
_audio: Every card is silent. Putting a bed under one is a licensing decision, the owner's alone.
